content.text:
I couldn't improve the drawing because there wasn't one. `0.svg` was just `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>`: no shapes, no size and no `viewBox`, so it showed a blank canvas. I went by the filename and turned it into a clean, scalable **0**:

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="64" height="64" viewBox="0 0 64 64" role="img">
  <title>0</title>
  <rect x="20" y="10" width="24" height="44" rx="12" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="6"/>
</svg>
```

- **Shape:** a narrow, rounded outline, centered with even margins. Keeping it narrow stops it looking like the letter O.
- **Scales cleanly:** the `viewBox` lets it resize without distortion, and it shows at 64×64 by default.
- **Matches text color:** `currentColor` makes it take the color of the surrounding text when you put it directly in HTML. Opened by itself it's black, so it's hard to see on a dark background.
- **Accessible:** `role="img"` and `<title>` give screen readers a label.
- **Easy to adjust:** change `stroke-width` to make the line thicker or thinner.

**I couldn't render it or validate it.** Checking which SVG tools were installed, validating the file with `xmllint`, and making a preview with Quick Look all needed approval, and nobody can approve anything in this session. Instead I checked the coordinates by hand: the shape sits fully inside the canvas with nothing cut off, and the markup is valid.

If `0.svg` was meant to hold something else, such as an export that came out blank, tell me what it should show and I'll make that instead.
